When the round ends, that's enough for today.

A round is short enough to finish within your break.

01How ipe makes games

ipe is short for idle process: the state a processor finally settles into when there is nothing left to do. The rest in ipe.rest comes from there. Our games are not meant to be quiet games. Strategy and duels still make you think. What connects them to rest is that a game should not take over your break, it should sit down inside it. The end of a round is clear, the rules do not ask for a long explanation, nothing nags you to log in or cuts in with an ad, and we say what we have promised and what we do not know yet.

Iltonggi

一統記

Coming soon iPhone first

A short, fast, classic territory-conquest strategy game set in Korea's Three Kingdoms era.

No ads, no tracking

What you will like

  1. One round that fits a break. A round takes 5 to 10 minutes, closing the app saves your game automatically, and nothing nags you to log in every day.
  2. A map you only know as far as you can see. Land you have not visited stays in the fog until you send a spy. You can step into a battle with direct command, or leave it to auto.
  3. A quiet, open app. It collects no personal information, has no ads or tracking, and its core features work offline. The game's site is available in 11 languages.

Not for you if

  1. If you want fast, real-time play. Iltonggi is turn-based, so the weight is on choosing where to strike, not on reaction speed.
  2. If you want to play on Android right now. The iPhone version comes first and other platforms will be announced later. The Three Kingdoms is a setting, not a history lesson: the game's terms say it may differ from historical fact.

View official site: Iltonggi → Blog: Making-of Terms of use

Inkisle

InkIsle

Coming soon iOS first, Android alongside

A light island-conquest strategy game for your phone: send fleets between islands and tint the sea your color.

Planned: every round free · no ads · optional help items

What you will like

  1. A few minutes, one hand. A round takes 3 to 5 minutes, and in portrait you just drag with your thumb. No account and no network needed.
  2. The rules fit on one page. Islands make troops, and a larger force arriving takes the island. So a won round does not drag on, it ends once you are clearly ahead.
  3. Readable even if you cannot tell the colors apart. Each side has its own color and flag shape. Clear a round and the next one opens, and every sea adds one rule.

Not for you if

  1. If you want a story and characters. Inkisle has no story on purpose. The fun is in taking islands and wanting to open the next sea.
  2. If you want slow turn-based play, or to compete online right now. A round flows in real time, and online play will be decided later, based on how players respond.

View official site: Inkisle → Journal: Making-of

Patchland

Claim It All

Coming soon iOS and Android

A quick, offline territory game played with paper patches. Win land from six quirky AI lords, one region at a time, in three ways: Trace, Place and Spread.

No ads, no subscription

What you will like

  1. Three ways to take land. Trace a line and come home to claim what you circle. Place stones on a hex board. Or pick a color and let it spread. Each mode plays differently.
  2. A map that grows with you. A 24-region paper map with a lord on every region. Boss lords play first to two wins, and your lands slowly gather pieces while you are away.
  3. A reason to come back each day. Today's Land is one board, the same for everyone, with a streak to keep. Collect all 24 lord cards in the Lord Album for free.

Not for you if

  1. If you want to play people online. Matches are against AI lords, and the game works offline.
  2. If you want a long story. The matches are short and light, built for quick sessions.

View official site: Patchland →

Claimball

Coming soon iOS and Android

A casual duel against an AI rival on a notebook grid. The tile where your ball bounces becomes your land. Miss, and you lose land.

Free to try. One purchase unlocks everything. No ads, no subscription.

What you will like

  1. About 90 seconds a match. It fits even a short gap, and the last seconds are a showdown. (A pre-launch proposal, so it may change.)
  2. A board you read at a glance. On a 6 by 10 notebook grid, your tiles and your rival's are split by color. A smash with the center of your paddle claims 3 tiles at once.
  3. Your rivals raise the level. At launch there are 6 AI rivals across 2 leagues (a pre-launch proposal, so it may change), with more planned in updates. Free to try. One purchase unlocks everything. No ads, no subscription.

Not for you if

  1. If busy-handed games are a burden. You return the ball in real time, so it differs from a game you can think through at leisure.
  2. If you want to play people online. Every match is you against an AI rival.

View official site: Claimball → Journal: Making-of Terms of use

Sunmeld

Space Merge Duel

Coming soon iOS and Android

A merge duel against an AI opponent in one shared tub. Drop a stone, merge matching stones into the next stage, and score. Overflow the tub and you lose.

Free to try, one purchase unlocks everything, no ads

What you will like

  1. Four lines of rules. Take turns dropping stones, matching stages merge, whoever merges scores, and if the tub overflows the player who placed the last stone loses.
  2. The shape you stack becomes your opponent's space. You share one tub, so there is a taste of working out what you leave behind.
  3. Every opponent has its own habits. The same tub plays out differently each time. It is free to try, one purchase unlocks everything, and there are no ads.

Not for you if

  1. If you want to build your own records or play against friends. Every match is a duel against an AI opponent, so it feels different from a puzzle where you chase a high score, or from playing people.
  2. If you expect a brand-new kind of game. Dropping and merging is a familiar kind of game. What is different here is the one tub you share and the AI you duel.

View official site: Sunmeld → Journal: Making-of Terms of use

Tottertop

Coming soon iOS and Android

A one-tap physics game. A swaying crane drops blocks, and you stack a tower that sways a little more with every block.

Free, with optional rewarded ads.

What you will like

  1. One tap is the whole game. The crane swings on its own; you tap to drop the block.
  2. About a minute a round. Short enough for a break, one round at a time.
  3. Free to play. No purchase needed; the only ads are optional rewarded ones.

Not for you if

  1. If you want a steady, precise tower. The crane and the tower both sway, so every block lands where the physics puts it.
  2. If you want to play other people. It is a solo game.

View official site: Tottertop →

Moss Garden

Coming soon iOS and Android

An idle garden for your phone. Plant eight kinds of plants, grow them, and gather the dew they leave behind.

Free, with optional rewarded ads.

What you will like

  1. Eight plants to tend. Plant and grow eight kinds of plants, and gather the dew each one leaves.
  2. A garden that changes with day and season. The background follows the time of day and the season.
  3. A garden you come back to. A field guide fills up plant by plant, and a prestige reset lets you start the garden over.

Not for you if

  1. If you want hands-on play all the time. It is an idle garden: the plants grow on their own, and you come back to gather the dew.
  2. If you want a large plant list. The garden has eight kinds of plants.

View official site: Moss Garden →

Dusk Blocks

Coming soon iOS TestFlight now, Android later

Drop 3 pieces on an 8x8 board and clear lines. A calm, one-handed block puzzle at dusk.

—

What you will like

  1. Three pieces, one board. You drop three pieces on an 8x8 board and clear the lines they complete. That is the whole loop, and it stays readable from the first round.
  2. Built for one hand. The game is set at dusk and built for one hand: a calm pace, and a round that fits inside a break.
  3. No account. There is no account to make, and the card says exactly where the release stands: the iOS build is on TestFlight, the store pages come after.

Not for you if

  1. If you want to play on Android right now. The iOS TestFlight build comes first, and the Android version is still in progress.
  2. If you want a finished feature list. It is still in testing, so features may change before release.

View official site: Dusk Blocks →

Bottled Marbles

Coming soon iOS TestFlight now, Android later

Sort colorful marbles into glass bottles. A calm, clear sorting puzzle.

—

What you will like

  1. Sorting is the whole game. The goal is plain to see: sort the colorful marbles into the right glass bottles. The game keeps it that way.
  2. Calm and clear. It is a sorting puzzle that stays calm and clear, meant to be played a few minutes at a time.
  3. No account. There is no account to make, and the card says exactly where the release stands: the iOS build is on TestFlight, the game's site is live.

Not for you if

  1. If you want to play on Android right now. The iOS TestFlight build comes first, and the Android version is still in progress.
  2. If you want a finished feature list. It is still in testing, so features may change before release.

07About ipe()

ipe() is a small AI-native studio that builds quiet things for busy minds. The name is short for idle process, and the studio says openly where it uses AI. This portal collects its games in one place. The studio's other product is idle, calm lo-fi music.
